title: Assert telemetry tests on a captured sink, not on a return value

facts.note: Telemetry colocation identifies a telemetry test.
Needs a file-content observer for a `Telemetry:` header or a TELEMETRY/EVENT/METRIC URN kind segment (the bun_telemetry_test validator does this).
Detector finding: telemetry test lacks toHaveBeenCalled[With|Times] or an expectation on .emit/.emitted/.capture/.track/.record.

fires: Writing or editing a *.telemetry.test.* file whose assertions only check the function's return value.
A test file with a `Telemetry:` header or TELEMETRY/EVENT/METRIC URN kind segment that never asserts on the emitter spy/mock/captured array.
doesNotFire: A non-telemetry test file (no Telemetry: header, no TELEMETRY/EVENT/METRIC URN kind, not *.telemetry.test.*) — the tester profile's own rule governs it.
Repositories that have not adopted this rule family (inert until adoption).
A telemetry test that already asserts with toHaveBeenCalledWith on the captured emitter.

given: A telemetry test: a test file with a `Telemetry:` header, a TELEMETRY/EVENT/METRIC URN kind segment, or *.telemetry.test.* colocation
when: the test is written or changed
then: The test asserts on the emission itself via the captured sink — `toHaveBeenCalled[With|Times]` or an expectation on `.emit` / `.emitted` / `.capture` / `.track` / `.record`.
prefer: Capture the emitter (spy, mock, or captured array the emitter writes to — the thing whose content is the emission), inject it into the unit under test, and assert on it.
Assert the exact event identity and payload on the sink (e.g. toHaveBeenCalledWith(<event URN>, <payload>)), joining the captured-sink and exact-identity requirements.
avoid: Asserting only on the function's return value — a return value is not a sink; it proves the function ran, not that the item fired.
Satisfying the detector with an emission-vocabulary expectation that does not inspect what the sink actually received.
unless: The test is not telemetry-identified; only telemetry-identified tests are scanned and the tester profile's own rule governs the rest.
The rule family has not been adopted in the repository (inert until adoption, like every rule in this family).
why: Dashboards, alerts and downstream analytics are built on the emission; a return-value check proves the function ran, not that the event fired — only the sink saw it fire.
evidence: The telemetry test file contains toHaveBeenCalled, toHaveBeenCalledWith or toHaveBeenCalledTimes, or an expect on .emit/.emitted/.capture/.track/.record.
The bun_telemetry_test validator reports no finding for the file.
verifier_detail: Telemetry test identification: `Telemetry:` header, a TELEMETRY/EVENT/METRIC URN kind segment, or *.telemetry.test.* colocation; non-identified tests are not scanned.

Predicate is deliberately the emission-assertion vocabulary (toHaveBeenCalled[With|Times]; expectations on .emit / .emitted / .capture / .track / .record), not a data-flow analysis: it names what a test must contain, not what the runtime did.
Term captured_sink: the spy, mock or captured array the emitter writes to — the thing whose CONTENT is the emission. A return value is not a sink.
Rule is inert until the repository adopts the family.
audit: Same obligation as tester.bun.telemetry-emit, carried into the telemetry profile and joined with the exact-identity requirement (graph: requires tester.bun.telemetry-emit).

sharedNodes.text: strict: atdd-bun fails on every finding; it has no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

additions.text: Satisfying the detector with an emission-vocabulary expectation that does not inspect what the sink actually received.
additions.justification: Metric-gaming guard: the vocabulary-based predicate (S017–S018) can be satisfied superficially; source intent (S012 'only the sink saw it fire') requires a real sink assertion.
